questions.question: Your vehicle breaks down on a public road. What should you do?

options.text: Stop where you are and turn on your hazard lights.
Stop where you are and hold down your horn.
Pull off the right side of the road and turn on your hazard lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and turn on your hazard lights.
questions.explanation: Pull off the right side of the road if you can. Turn on your hazard lights so other drivers can see your vehicle while you wait for help.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A downward-facing triangle is a yield sign. Be ready to slow down or stop when you see this sign.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is using its siren and flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Stop immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to emergency vehicles with sirens and flashing lights. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop. Avoid stopping in an intersection. You can move again after the emergency vehicle passes.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing a vehicle?

options.text: When the driver you passed signals for you to return.
After you signal for three seconds.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure you have enough space before returning to your lane. Check your rearview mirror. When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle, you have enough room to return safely.

questions.question: How should you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Check only the left outside mirror.
Look over your left or right shoulder.
Check only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check the blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: On a multilane one-way street, which lane should you use to turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: Any lane (as long as it is safe).
The leftmost lane.
The center lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The leftmost lane.
questions.explanation: Start your left turn from the leftmost lane of the road.

questions.question: Another driver is passing you in a no passing zone. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep the same speed and position.
Slow down so the other driver can safely return to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down so the other driver can safely return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Slow down to help the passing driver return to your lane safely. This helps everyone avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: Your vehicle has a two-part seat belt system. How should you use it?

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
questions.explanation: Always wear both parts of a two-part seat belt system. Using only one part reduces your protection. Even if you have an automatic shoulder belt, fasten your lap belt as well.

questions.question: When can you drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
If there are two or more lanes in your direction.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never drive off the road onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When turning left, who must you yield to?

options.text: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
Passing cars.
No one in particular.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to all vehicles coming from the opposite direction. This includes bicycles and motorcycles.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in work zones?

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as possible.
Keep a safe distance between your vehicle and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance between your vehicle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, keep a safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Do not tailgate. Increase your following distance.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on snow or ice?

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Change your speed and direction slowly and smoothly.
Drive the same way you would on dry roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your speed and direction slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, make slow and smooth changes to your speed and direction. Do not use cruise control on snow or ice. Your tires may slip, and you will lose control.

questions.question: A vehicle is entering the interstate from an entrance ramp into your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass them.
Change lanes to give them room to merge safely.
Ignore them because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to give them room to merge safely.
questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering the interstate. Change lanes when possible so they can merge smoothly and safely.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in construction and work zones?

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers mark work zones. Use extra caution when you see orange warning signs on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road ahead.
Do not enter.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves ahead.

questions.question: What should a driver do about the right-of-way?

options.text: Assume all drivers obey right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Right-of-way rules guide who should yield at an intersection, but do not assume you automatically have it. Consider the situation and conditions. Yield your right-of-way if it helps prevent a collision.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?

options.text: Speed up to get through quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Keep your normal speed throughout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down and be prepared to stop. Follow posted speed limits and watch for workers and changing conditions.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street, where should you position your vehicle?

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the center line.
On the left side of the center line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the center line.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, stay in the lane closest to the center line. Turn just before your car reaches the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: A driver behind you wants to pass. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Reduce your speed to help them pass.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed to help them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver wants to pass you, ease off the accelerator to help them. You may need to slow down so they can pass safely and return to your lane.

questions.question: How far should your chest be from the center of the steering wheel?

options.text: 10 to 12 inches
5 inches
20 inches

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 to 12 inches
questions.explanation: Adjust your seat so you can see 12 to 15 feet ahead. Your chest should be 10 to 12 inches from the steering wheel center. Your shoulders should be at the same height as the top of the steering wheel.

questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle skids to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Do not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left.
Turn your steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: If you skid on a wet or icy road, remove your foot from the accelerator and avoid using the brakes. Turn your steering wheel in the direction the rear is skidding. If your vehicle has anti-lock brakes, press the brakes firmly and steer straight ahead.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Keep a larger distance between your vehicle and the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger distance between your vehicle and the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Keep at least a three- to four-second distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop very quickly. Following too closely puts both you and the rider in danger. If the rider falls, you need extra space to avoid hitting them. Falls are most likely on wet or icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges or railroad tracks.

questions.question: You should check your rearview mirrors:

options.text: Often to watch traffic moving behind you.
Only to see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to watch traffic moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Do not stare at one spot while driving. Check your rearview mirrors often so you know where nearby vehicles are.

questions.question: If dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should drive slowly and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly. Other drivers may also have trouble seeing you.

questions.question: As daylight fades, you should use your:

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
Emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams when daylight begins to fade so others can see you. Only use high beams in open areas with no other drivers nearby.

questions.question: Why should drivers give children on bicycles extra space?

options.text: They do not have the same reflexes as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see than adults.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Be aware that children on bikes may suddenly ride from the sidewalk onto the road.

questions.question: In heavy fog, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: Before backing up your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check behind the vehicle before getting in.
Only use your mirrors.
Accelerate quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before getting in.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before getting in. Children and small objects may be impossible to see from the driver's seat.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels, causing loss of steering control.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels, causing loss of steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock the front wheels and cause you to lose steering control. Drive at a safe speed for the conditions to avoid needing hard braking.

questions.question: Your vehicle's wheels have run off the edge of the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to get back on the pavement.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
Apply the brakes and turn the front wheels sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, grip the steering wheel firmly and release the gas pedal. Apply the brakes gently. Once your speed drops, check traffic and find a safe place to return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel sharply, as this can cause you to lose control or enter other lanes.
